claim: Defines the finite discrete-time domain T as the integer set {0, 1, ..., N_T-1} on which position signals are sampled.
Defines the position signal p as a scalar function from the discrete-time domain T to the reals, the recorded output of individuals performing repetitive motor tasks.
Defines the velocity v(t) of a position signal as the backward finite difference of position divided by the sampling time, with v(0) = 0.
Defines w_1, w_2 as velocity profiles: functions from the velocity domain V to [0, 1].
Defines W_1, W_2 as the cumulative distribution functions of the two velocity profiles w_1, w_2.

Defines the earth mover's distance (1-Wasserstein distance) between two velocity profiles as the sum over the velocity domain of the absolute differences of their cumulative distribution functions times the bin width.
Defines the dissimilarity matrix Delta as a nonnegative n-by-n real matrix used to project velocity profiles into the two-dimensional similarity plane via classical metric multidimensional scaling.
Defines each entry Delta_ij of the dissimilarity matrix as the earth mover's distance between velocity profiles w_i and w_j.
Defines the velocity signal v as a scalar function from the discrete-time domain T to the reals.

Defines the positive and negative amplitude envelopes A_p^+(t), A_p^-(t) of a position signal: each envelope tracks p(t) at velocity zero-crossings of the corresponding lobe and holds its previous value otherwise, as a complementary descriptor of individual motor signatures.
equation: A_p^+(t) \coloneqq \begin{dcases} p(t), & \text{if } v(t) \le 0, v(t-1) > 0, p(t) > 0,\\ A_p^+(t-1), & \text{otherwise}, \end{dcases} \\ A_p^-(t) \coloneqq \begin{dcases} p(t), & \text{if } v(t) \ge 0, v(t-1) < 0, p(t) < 0,\\ A_p^-(t-1), & \text{otherwise}, \end{dcases}

claim: Defines the mean positive and mean negative amplitudes of a position signal as the time averages of its amplitude envelopes over the discrete-time domain.
Defines the first-order low-pass filtered velocity estimate as an exponential moving average of the sampled velocity with filter gain beta in (0,1).
Defines the generated position update: the new position equals the previous position plus the sampling time times the filtered velocity estimate.

Defines the prediction loss L_pred as the negative log-likelihood of the target velocity under the predicted Gaussian distribution: one half the log of the predicted variance plus the squared standardized residual.
Defines the generation loss L_gen as the mean earth mover's distance between each participant signal's velocity profile and the corresponding generated profile; the optimal model weights minimize it.

Defines the four profile collections that comparison sets A and B range over: P_i (participant i's human velocity profiles), G_i (model i's generated profiles), P_neg-i (all other humans' profiles), and G_neg-i (all other models' profiles).
equation: A,B \in \{P_{i}, G_{i}, P_{\neg i}, G_{\neg i}\}

claim: Defines delta^em(A,B) as the set of pairwise earth mover's distances between distinct elements of profile sets A and B, and delta^{em,epsilon}(A,B) as the same set with each distance inflated by a (1+epsilon) tolerance margin.
equation: \begin{aligned} \delta^{\mathrm{em}}(A, B) \coloneqq & \{\delta^{\mathrm{em}}(w_1, w_2) \mid w_1 \in A, w_2 \in B, w_1 \neq w_2 \},\\ \delta^{\mathrm{em},\epsilon}(A, B) \coloneqq & \{(1+\epsilon)\delta^{\mathrm{em}}(w_1, w_2) \mid \\ &\qquad\qquad\qquad w_1 \in A, w_2 \in B,w_1 \neq w_2 \}, \end{aligned}

claim: Defines the average earth mover's distance delta^em_avg(A,B) as the arithmetic mean of the pairwise EMD set between profile sets A and B.
Hypothesis H1 (well-posed individual motor signatures): the average EMD among participant i's own signals is no larger than between participant i's signals and other participants' signals.

Hypothesis H2 (fidelity): the average EMD between participant i's signals and model i's generated signals is within tolerance epsilon of participant i's own intra-individual distance, so the model reproduces the individual's motor signature.
Hypothesis H3 (distinct models): the average EMD among model i's generated signals is no larger than between model i's and other models' signals, so each model exhibits a distinct signature.
Hypothesis H4 (person-to-model specificity): participant i's signals are at least as similar to the corresponding model i's generated signals as to other models' signals.

Hypothesis H5 (model-to-person specificity): model i's generated signals are at least as similar to the corresponding participant i's signals as to other participants' signals, so the model captures the target's signature rather than generic human motion.
Defines the fidelity-test tolerance margin epsilon as the ratio of the jackknife standard error SE_i to the reference intra-individual average EMD.
Defines the jackknife leave-one-out mean as the average pairwise EMD over all signal pairs excluding signal k.
Defines the jackknife overall mean as the average of the leave-one-out means over all n_s signals.
Defines the jackknife standard error SE_i as the square root of (n_s-1)/n_s times the sum of squared deviations of the leave-one-out means from their overall mean.

Defines the nearest target signal of a generated profile as its EMD argmin over participant i's recordings, and gamma^{G-P} as that minimum EMD distance; used to verify generated signals are not pathologically close copies of recordings.
Defines gamma^{P-P} as the EMD from the nearest target signal to its own nearest distinct neighbor within participant i's recordings, the baseline intra-individual spacing.

Defines the replay-check ratio rho^{G_i} as the average over generated signals of the distance to the nearest target recording divided by that recording's distance to its nearest fellow recording; rho near 1 means natural spacing while rho much below 1 means pathological copying.
Defines the mean-amplitude distance delta^a between two position signals as the Euclidean distance between their (mean positive amplitude, mean negative amplitude) pairs.
Defines delta^a(A,B) as the set of pairwise mean-amplitude distances between distinct elements of signal sets A and B, and the epsilon-inflated variant delta^{a,epsilon}(A,B).
equation: \begin{aligned} \delta^{\mathrm{a}}(A, B) &\coloneqq \{\delta^{\mathrm{a}}(p_1, p_2) \mid p_1 \in A, p_2 \in B, p_1 \ne p_2 \},\\ \delta^{\mathrm{a},\epsilon}(A, B) &\coloneqq \{(1+\epsilon)\delta^{\mathrm{a}}(p_1, p_2) \mid p_1 \in A, p_2 \in B, p_1 \ne p_2 \}, \end{aligned}

claim: Defines the average mean-amplitude distance delta^a_avg(A,B) as the arithmetic mean of the pairwise amplitude-distance set.
Defines the amplitude-space fidelity tolerance epsilon as the ratio of the jackknife standard error to the reference intra-individual average amplitude distance.

Defines the overlap Omega_ij between individuals i and j as the intersection-over-union (Jaccard index) of their similarity-plane ellipses under Lebesgue measure; small overlap indicates distinct motor behaviors.
Defines the center distance delta_ij as the Euclidean (L2) distance between the ellipse centers of individuals i and j, a complementary similarity measure for small nearby ellipses with zero overlap.

Defines the harmonic oscillator's position as p(t) = A sin(omega t) with amplitude A and angular frequency omega, parametrized to match the average amplitude and frequency of the human position signal.
Defines the oscillator's velocity as the time derivative of its position, v(t) = A omega cos(omega t).
Defines g as the velocity transformation mapping time t to velocity v.
Defines g^{-1} as the inverse velocity transformation mapping velocity v back to time t, wherever it exists.
Defines the time density f_T as uniform with density omega/pi on the monotone interval [0, pi/omega] and zero elsewhere.
Defines the inverse velocity law t = g^{-1}(v) = (1/omega) arccos(v/(A omega)) for v in [-A omega, A omega].

Derives the harmonic oscillator's velocity profile (probability density) f_V(v) = 1/(pi A omega sqrt(1-(v/(A omega))^2)) by applying the random-variable transformation law to the uniform time density.
Defines the symbol Pi as 2 pi/omega, the full oscillation period of the harmonic oscillator.
